messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: standard errors for IRTpars=T
parts:
Hi Phillip

I am working in a model, I used the IRT parametrisation, but I cannot get the standard error for the b parameters, how can I get the standard error for b?

If mirt doesnt give it, what would be the transformation from the standard error of d?


Thanks

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: standard errors for IRTpars=T
parts:
If you are in the fortunate circumstance where you used a Rasch model, the SE for b and d will be the same. If not though, you'd need to transform the standard errors using the delta method, which is something I haven't gotten around to yet (it's not high on my priority list). 

It's possible to write your own IRT models with the createItem() function to get them if you are that desperate, or, last I checked, the ltm package implemented the delta method for these models and should work for you needs. Cheers.

Phil

parts:
Hi Phillip

Lets say I am desperate (not really, but lets me learn more), and I want to use the createitem functions. I can easily create a 3PL like follow
name <- 'old3PL'
par <- c(a = .5, b = -2, c=.1)
est <- c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)
P.old3PL <- function(par,Theta, ncat){
  a <- par[1]
  b <- par[2]
  c <- par[3]
  P1 <- c+(1-c) * (1 / (1 + exp(-1*a*(Theta - b))) )
  cbind(1-P1, P1)
}

x <- createItem(name, par=par, est=est, P=P.old3PL)

But I also need a graded response model, I tried to code it, but didnt work, could you help me to make it work?

This is my code
name <- 'oldgrm'
par <- c(a = .5, b1 = -2, b2=0, b3=1)
est <- c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)
P.oldgrm <- function(par,Theta, ncat){
  a <- par[1]
  b1 <- par[2]
  b2 <- par[2]
  b3 <- par[2]
  P1 <- (1 / (1 + exp(-1*a*(Theta - b1))) )
  P2 <- (1 / (1 + exp(-1*a*(Theta - b2))) )
  P3 <- (1 / (1 + exp(-1*a*(Theta - b3))) )
  cbind(1-P1, P1,1-P2, P2,1-P3, P3)
}

xi <- createItem(name, par=par, est=est, P=P.oldgrm)

SPECS <- mirt.model('F = 1-20
PRIOR = (1-20, a, lnorm, 0, 1),
(1-20,  b1,  norm, 0, 2),
(1-20,  b2,  norm, 0, 2),
(1-20,  b3,  norm, 0, 2)')

sv <- mirt(data=x, model=SPECS, itemtype='oldgrm', customItems=list(oldgrm=xi), pars = 'values')
tail(sv) #looks good
mod <- mirt(x, SPECS,  'oldgrm', customItems=list(oldgrm=xi),SE=T)

This gives me this error
> mod <- mirt(x, SPECS,  'oldgrm', customItems=list(oldgrm=xi),SE=T)
Error in computeItemtrace(pars = pars, Theta = Theta, itemloc = itemloc,  : 
  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

Appreciate any help

bye

P.oldgrm <- function(par,Theta, ncat){

There is way too many response curves here. With 3 intercepts there should only be 4 probably trace lines. You might want to recheck the math to see what is going on here (they don't quite look to be ordered). Also, you'll definitely want to put these starting values very close to the maximum likelihood estimates since nothing stops the b parameters from going 'out of order' in the customItem() definitions. So, the estimation could crash if it's too far away from the maximum. 

Phil

parts:
Hi Phillip

Here I am writing directly the equations from Samejima (for variables with 4 categories)

name <- 'oldgrm'
par <- c(a1 = .5, b1 = -2, b2=0, b3=2)

est <- c(TRUE, TRUE, TRUE, TRUE)

P.oldgrm <- function(par,Theta,ncat){
a1 <- par[1]

b1 <- par[2]
  b2 <- par[2]
  b3 <- par[2]

P4 <- (1 / (1 + exp(-1*a1*(Theta - b3))) )
  P3 <- (1 / (1 + exp(-1*a1*(Theta - b2))) ) - P4
  P2 <- (1 / (1 + exp(-1*a1*(Theta - b1))) ) - (P3+P4)
  P1 <- 1 - (P2+P3+P4)

  return(cbind(1-P1,1-P2, P2,1-P3, P3,1-P4, P4))

}

xi <- createItem(name, par=par, est=est, P=P.oldgrm)
When I check the values it seems right to me

> sv <- mirt(data=x, model=SPECS, itemtype='oldgrm', customItems=list(oldgrm=xi), pars = 'values')
> tail(sv) #looks good

82   all GROUP GroupPars COV_11     82   1.0  1e-04    Inf FALSE       none     NaN     NaN


But when I try to estimate the model I get this error, taht I dont understand how to overcome
> mod <- mirt(x, 1,  itemtype='oldgrm', customItems=list(oldgrm=xi),SE=T)

  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

Any help to fix this error is appreciated

thanks
